sentences.text: Avimimus was a compact dinosaur standing about 45 centimeters tall at the hip and reaching roughly 1.6 meters in total length.
Although its head was small compared to its body, the creature possessed a large brain and enormous eye sockets.
Instead of teeth, the animal had a horny beak similar to that of parrots, with tooth-like projections at the tip of the premaxilla.
Bumps on the ulna were confirmed in 1987, yet their specific purpose remains unclear despite reports of a keel and other structures.
Large bones surrounded the cranial cavity to protect the brain, a feature consistent with its unusually large brain size.
The ilium was oriented almost horizontally, creating exceptionally wide hips that differed from other similar dinosaurs.
Long tibiae relative to the femurs indicate a body plan adapted for running.
Dr. Sergei Kurzanov officially described the species in 1981 after Russian paleontologists recovered the fossils.
The initial specimens were found in the Djadokhta Formation before being formally named Avimimus portentosus.
A new species, Avimimus nemegtensis, was formally described in 2018 based on material identified earlier.
Footprints in the same area likely belonged to the animal, offering clues about its movement.
Bonebeds suggest the animals were buried quickly by rapid water flow and then reburied a short distance away.
While Kurzanov suggested weak flight might be possible, most paleontologists today do not believe the animal could fly.
Originally, the unique set of avian characteristics led scientists to consider it a very close relative of birds.
Later phylogenetic analyses did not support this view, and modern scientists now classify it within the diverse group of primitive bird-like dinosaurs known as oviraptorosaurs.
Recent studies place Avimimus within the family Oviraptoridae and the subgroup Elmisaurinae.
The dinosaur lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Campanian stage in what is now Asia, specifically in the Barun Goyot Formation.
At that time, the area featured an arid environment with sand dune fields and only intermittent water currents.
It coexisted with other dinosaurs such as the tyrannosaurid Tarbosaurus and the hadrosaurid Saurolophus in the Nemegt Formation.
It is debated whether Avimimus originated from the Djadokhta Formation as originally thought, with evidence suggesting it likely hailed from the more recent Nemegt Formation.
There is a debate regarding the diet; while the toothless beak suggests herbivory or omnivory, Kurzanov hypothesized it was an insectivore.
